The continuum emission of the binary component, Source A, reveals the substructure consisting of 5 intensity peaks within 100 au from the protostar.

The positions of two continuum peaks (A1 and A2) are consistent with those previously observed at cm wavelength, if their proper motions are considered. They also agree with the recent report on the 3 mm continuum emission. We also detect new continuum peaks (A3, A4, and A1a).

The C 17 O emission mainly traces the circummultiple structure on a 300 au scale centered at the intensity centroid of the continuum, while it is very weak within the radius of 50 au from the centroid.

The H 2 CS emission, in contrast, traces the rotating disk structure around one of the continuum peaks (A1). Thus, it seems that the rotation centroid of the circummultiple structure is slightly different from that of the disk around A1.

all_quotes.quote: As well, the difference of the systemic velocity between the two models, 3.9 km s − 1 for the circummultiple structure and 2.5 km s − 1 for the circumstellar structure, implies a potential motion of the protostar A1 in Source A.

It is likely due to a local accretion shock and/or the preferential protostellar heating of the transition zone from the circummultiple structure to the disk around A1.
